title: Token-degradation attribution and multi-region shed decision dashboard
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We frequently see tail token-latency spikes after load shifts or partial regional contention. Current dashboards surface aggregated p99/p999 token times but do not explain whether regressions are driven by KV-cache miss storms, kernel contention, intra-shard queuing, or cross-region retries. This makes it hard for oncall and SREs to distinguish incidents that require capacity vs. those that require routing/circuit adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New token-degradation dashboard in Grafana that attributes tail token latency to orthogonal signal sources: kv_cache_miss_rate, early_batch_queue_depth, kernel_saturation_ratio, cross_region_retry_ratio.
A2: Circuit-breaker decision telemetry added: rwin_shed_decision{region,reason,variant} counter and rwin_shed_duration_seconds histogram; visible as rollup panels in the dashboard.
A3: Region-prioritized failover heatmap that shows per-region SLO burn rate and the percentage of traffic routed to fallback variants during the last 30m/6h/24h windows.

A4: Synthetic token-trace generator (short sequences) producing tagged traces that surface per-token timing across KV lookup, attention kernel, and network hop; integrated into the dashboard sample view.

A5: Playbook snippets in the dashboard linking from panels to runbook steps for the most common attribution patterns (e.g., high kv miss + low kernel saturation => increase prefix cache; high kernel saturation + queue depth increase => scale pool).
notes: Design goals: enable fast root-cause hypothesis in first 2 minutes of paging; minimize cardinality explosion in metrics. Use histograms + t-digest rollups rather than per-sequence labels where possible.
Telemetry approach: add a lightweight token-latency span annotation at the serving runtime boundary and emit aggregated distributions per model_variant/region/sequence_length_bucket.
Metric naming convention proposed: rwin_token_latency_ms_bucket, rwin_token_latency_tdigest, rwin_kv_cache_hit_ratio, rwin_kernel_saturation, rwin_shed_decision_total.
Sampling: full token-level traces are too expensive; enable 0.5% deterministic sampling per request for traces and keep aggregated histograms at 100% with 1ms bucketing up to 500ms and coarse beyond.

Cost trade-offs: retaining full token histograms for every model/region will increase metrics cardinality; initial rollout limited to top 5 customer-facing models and to dedicated clusters for 48h before broader rollout.
Rollout strategy: feature-flagged GNMT telemetry toggle per cluster; start with non-prod and canary reg-prod then widen to all regions.
Related work: ties into the routing fallback policies in runtime-1.21 and the SLO propagation work in ENG-32345.
required_work: Runtime: emit rwin_token_latency_tdigest and rwin_token_stage_durations with model_variant and region tags.
Telem pipeline: add t-digest aggregator into metrics ingestion to support p50/p90/p99/p999 queries efficiently.
Dashboard: assemble attribution panels and a compact summary row for oncall with quick links.
Synthetic traces: small generator service and test harness to produce representative 8-32 token sequences with varying KV prefix hit patterns.
Playbook & docs: author initial runbook entries and oncall quick actions for the dashboard patterns.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary 48h): enable telemetry on canary runtime cluster in us-west-2 for top 3 variants; validate ingestion and dashboard panels.
Phase 1 (reg-prod): enable on 2 additional regions and open to SRE + runtime oncall; measure metric cardinality and cost.
Phase 2 (global): enable sampling rules and lower t-digest resolution only if cost exceeds budget; ship dashboard to default oncall home dashboard.
Rollback: disable telemetry flag and backfill heuristics to reconstruct prior dashboards if gaps occur.
